summary: Provisional warmup credit misallocated after quantized-variant fallback during dedicated rollover
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightLearn reports unexpected debit lines on their March 1 invoice labeled as 'probe-warmup' and a missing provisional warmup credit that should have offset those charges. This occurred during a scheduled dedicated rollover where their canary traffic exercised a quantized model variant and several requests fell back to hosted variants.

Impact:
- Finalized invoice shows a $2,430 line item for 'probe-warmup' and no corresponding provisional warmup credit.
- Usage appears attributed to the parent cost center (brightlearn-prod) rather than the intended project (brightlearn-staging), causing an incorrect charge on production invoice.
- Customer reports this jeopardizes their month-end reconciliation and they have requested an expedited adjustment.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dlx-dedicated-08 (us-east)
- Time window: 2026-03-01 01:15-02:20 UTC (rollover window)
- Models involved: llama-2-70b-quantized (canary), fallback to hosted redwood-open-13b-quant

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Trigger a scheduled warmup/batch run against deployed dedicated capacity using quantized variant.
2) Simulate partial capacity saturation so some microbatches are routed to hosted fallback.
3) Observe invoice postback for warmup events and provisional-credit assignment after cycle close.

Relevant logs / identifiers provided by customer:
- Example request IDs: rq_4b8f2a1c, rq_4b8f2a2d, rq_4b8f2a9f
- Billing fingerprint on invoice: bill_fp_20260301_uw1
- Postback payload sample (sanitized) attached in ticket: postback_20260301.json

Customer expectation:
- Warmup buffer credits should apply automatically to warmup events during rollover and be visible on the provisional invoice.
- Any warmup or probe traffic originating from the canary should be tagged and billed to the canary’s staging project, not to prod.

Requested outcome:
- Immediate provisional credit to offset the $2,430 line item and an invoice memo explaining the adjustment.
- Root-cause explanation and mitigation to avoid recurrence during future dedicated rollovers.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Priya Shah (Support): Acknowledged ticket and requested billing artifacts and postback samples. Asked for PID of the dedicated pool and any scheduled rollout notes.

2026-03-10 11:03 - BrightLearn (Customer): Sent postback sample and three example request IDs. Clarified that the canary used a truncated org tag: 'brightlearn-prod' and 'brightlearn-prod-legacy' were both active during the window.

2026-03-10 14:40 - Ethan Morales (SRE): Investigating rate-selector logs and postback reconciler. Noted several postbacks were tagged as 'probe-warmth' and attributed to parent org. Raised hypothesis about tag normalization/truncation in the reconciler. Linking internal team.

2026-03-11 08:21 - Billing (Support Ops): Temporarily applied a provisional credit of $2,430 to customer's account (pending final reconciliation). Noted this will appear as a credit memo; final invoice adjustment requires internal change and runbook action.
2026-03-12 10:02 - Ethan Morales (SRE): Confirmed root-cause and created INT-55012 for permanent fix. Leaving next steps in resolution.
investigation_notes:
Summary of investigation:
- Reconciler replayed postbacks for the window and discovered that tag normalization logic truncates tags >32 chars which caused 'brightlearn-prod-legacy' and 'brightlearn-prod' to collapse to the same namespace for rate-selector evaluation.
- Rate-selector cache flush occurred at 01:12 UTC as part of the rollover; during the transient, microbatches routed to hosted fallback generated postbacks with tag fingerprint 'brightlearn-prod' only.
- Postback-reconciler matched those events against the parent cost-center due to the truncated tag and therefore did not apply the provisional warmup buffer which is scoped to the staging project.
- No evidence of duplicate event replay; counts align. The issue is misattribution rather than duplicate metering.
- Reproducer: running reconciler locally with full tag strings and with the truncation rule reproduces misallocation.

Hypothesis: truncation + cache flush during rollover created a narrow window where hosted fallback postbacks lost the project suffix resulting in misattribution of warmup charges.
resolution:
Workaround and resolution steps taken:
1) Applied provisional credit of $2,430 to BrightLearn's billing account on 2026-03-11 (billing ticket memo BT-20260311-09). This offsets the disputed line item pending final reconciliation.
2) Opened INT-55012 to remove tag truncation at the reconciler boundary and harden rate-selector cache behavior during rollovers. Patch scheduled (rate-selector v1.7.2) and targeted for staged deploy on 2026-03-18 with a canary.
3) Manual run of postback-reconciler for 2026-03-01 window to reassign affected events to staging project and prepare invoice memo for finance.
4) Follow-up: Support will send BrightLearn a one-page incident explainer and the timeline once INT-55012 is validated in staging.
5) Owner: Ethan Morales (SRE) for technical fix, Billing Ops for final invoice credit.

Status: provisional credit applied. Permanent fix in progress (INT-55012). Will update when patch is deployed and finance issues final memo.
